title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Over a non-reduced base the claim that the geometric fibres' graphs 'form' a finite étale scheme in maquettes is not automatic. Example: a first-order smoothing xy = ε over k[ε] has a geometric fibre of type G, but its singular locus Spec k is not flat, let alone étale, over k[ε]. So 'type G' defined fibrewise only gives the reduced stratum. One must either restrict to reduced 𝕊 or define the stratum scheme-theoretically (nodes persisting, i.e. the local smoothing parameters vanish). Grothendieck's switch to 'courbes standard' in the last paragraph seems designed to handle exactly this, but on this page the gap is not addressed.
Minor notational overload: S is used both for the base and for the vertex set (the image distinguishes the base 𝕊 from the underlined vertex scheme S).

ideas.what: Dual graph of a family of stable curves as a locally constant étale sheaf ('schéma en maquettes') of graphs over the base, étale-locally constant.
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy of the dual graph / étale sheaf of dual graphs on a boundary stratum
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Deligne–Mumford (1969) and Knudsen (1983); made explicit later, e.g. in log/tropical work (Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne 2015) and in treatments of strata
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the stratification of M̄_{g,ν} 'à l'infini' qualitatively; no such formal definition is published

ideas.what: G-pinnings (isomorphisms of the dual graph with a fixed graph G) form a torsor under the finite constant group Aut G.
ideas.modern_name: Twisted forms classified by H^1(S, Aut G); the stratum M_G = [M̃_G / Aut G]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (descent theory); in moduli of curves, folklore in Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths and Graber–Pandharipande

ideas.what: Groupoid of standard G-pinned curves equivalent to the product over vertices of M_{g_α, I_α ⊔ Ã_α} (the half-edges at α become extra marked points).
ideas.modern_name: Product description of boundary strata / clutching morphisms ∏ M̄_{g_v,n_v} → M̄_{g,n}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the 'tour de Teichmüller' built from gluing of M_{g,ν}, not this precise statement

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, early, functorial formulation of boundary strata: the étale sheaf of dual graphs, the Aut G-torsor of pinnings, and the product decomposition. All of it is standard in the later literature (Knudsen, ACG, Getzler–Kapranov), so nothing a specialist would find new. It is mainly of historical interest as Grothendieck's private foundations for the Teichmüller tower.
